title: AI Factory
blurb: Run a whole AI company. Take a product from raw data to launch — every choice along the line matters.
objectives: That machine learning is a process, not one step
How the stages connect: collect, clean, train, test, deploy
Why early shortcuts cause expensive problems later

glossary.def: The full assembly line of an AI product, from data to launch and beyond.
Release the model so real people use it.
Keep watching after launch to catch new problems.
When a model gets worse over time because the world changed since it was trained.

steps.title: You inherit an AI company
steps.body:
Congratulations — you're the new boss of a struggling AI company. The board wants one thing: a **successful AI product**.

Here's the catch. A great model isn't one magic step. It's a whole **pipeline**: collect data, clean it, train, test, deploy, and keep watching. Mess up early and you'll pay for it later.

steps.title: Where do problems start?
steps.prompt: A deployed AI product is making bad predictions. Where did the trouble most likely begin?
choices: Only at the very last step
Earlier in the pipeline — like rushed data or skipped testing
steps.afterPick: Usually upstream. A shortcut in collecting or cleaning quietly becomes a disaster after launch. Let's run the line. →

steps.title: Run the line
steps.youWillDo: make a choice at each stage, then deploy
steps.body: Move your product through each stage — **Collect → Clean → Train → Test → Deploy**. Make a choice at each one, watch the **health** score, then **Deploy & monitor** to see how it does in the real world. Try a few runs and compare your launches.

steps.title: Every stage connects
steps.body:
Notice how choices **stacked up**. Cheap data plus skipped cleaning didn't just cost a little — it compounded, and a fancy model made it worse by memorizing the junk.

That's the big idea: machine learning is a **process**. Success depends on every stage working together, not one heroic step.

steps.title: The big picture
steps.question: What's the most accurate way to describe building an AI product?
choices: Just train a model and you're done
A connected process where every stage affects the final result
steps.explain: Collect → clean → train → test → deploy → monitor. Each stage feeds the next, and shortcuts travel downstream.

steps.title: Say it your way
steps.prompt: You've now trained models, cleaned data, set rewards, and shipped a product. In your own words: why is building good AI more than just 'making a smart model'?
steps.placeholder: Because a good AI product also needs…

recall.question: A successful AI product depends most on…
recall.explain: Every stage matters — that's the lifecycle of real machine learning.

steps.title: You ran the whole factory 🎉
steps.body:
You just did what real AI teams do: take a product through its **entire lifecycle**, balancing speed, cost, and quality at every step.

And you've now seen the big picture of AI — how it **learns from examples**, **explores with rewards**, **depends on clean, fair data**, **follows clear instructions**, and **costs real energy to run**. That's not just *using* AI — that's understanding *why it behaves the way it does*. 🏆
